record_identity.title: Gemini image-generation tuning produced historically inaccurate depictions and over-broad refusals

incident_identity.date_basis: AIID records 21 February 2024 for the incident cluster; Google paused people-image generation and published its postmortem on 23 February 2024.

summary: Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after users surfaced historically inaccurate and offensive outputs. Google later explained that diversity tuning failed to account for contexts where diversity should not be introduced and that the model also became more cautious than intended, refusing some benign prompts.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Google states that its tuning to produce diverse people did not correctly distinguish historical or otherwise specific contexts and that the model overcompensated. Google temporarily disabled people-image generation and committed to further testing. AIID Incident 645 aggregates 35 reports around the same failure cluster. Google’s 28 August 2024 update describes a staged rollout of renewed people-image generation with Imagen 3. This bounds the period of withdrawn functionality without proving universal restoration or repaired calibration.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A protective and diversity-oriented control became operative in contexts where its valid conditions were not satisfied and also over-triggered refusals on benign requests. This is a strong example of a safeguard/tuning objective activating outside its appropriate scope. Inappropriate triggering is distinct from control nonactivation. Pausing and proposed changes are response evidence, without proof of restored calibration. Later GAI Profile, development Profile and EU requirements are not retrospective, and standalone image generation is not runtime-agent dispatch. The provider’s pause is Aligned with the AI RMF disengagement requirement. The pause does not establish repaired generation quality. Harm Impact: Google withdrew the live people-image generation function and described a staged replacement months later. The actual loss of this product function supports material bounded service impairment. It was not an essential service, and elapsed months alone do not support S4.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows why protective controls need proportionate trigger conditions. A safeguard can pursue a legitimate objective yet still cause harm or loss of utility when it activates outside the circumstances that justify it, including by producing inaccurate historical depictions or refusing benign requests.
assessment_boundaries: The record does not treat diversity objectives themselves as a failure; the failure is the control's application in contexts where Google says it should not have applied.
The Incident does not adjudicate political claims about bias beyond Google's own acknowledgement of inaccurate historical outputs and over-conservative refusals.
Individual affected users and downstream reliance are not quantified.

The public account does not localise the implementation defect. No positively evidenced upstream misclassification with otherwise correct control activation is established; that hypothetical architecture does not defeat the observed benign-request refusal finding.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Describe source-backed material actions and response phases. Separate overlapping activity and attributed claims where exact sequence is not public.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Google launched people-image generation in the Gemini conversational app using Imagen 2. It described tuning intended to avoid harmful images and broaden representation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The product, intended function and safeguard purpose precede the observed tuning defect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Google reported diversity/safety tuning becoming operative in contexts where it should not have applied. The explicit absent-valid-trigger exclusion defeats activation failure and Boundary. The known result is inappropriate activation, already represented by Control Activation Validity.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Google reported that representation tuning overcompensated in historically or culturally specific requests, while excessive caution caused benign prompts to be refused. These were different reported effects, not two descriptions of separate identical requests.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A safeguard must become operative on a valid trigger and applicability basis; inappropriate activation differs from absent activation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Google acknowledged that its safeguards refused benign image prompts through excessive caution. The intended harmful-request condition was absent in those requests, yet refusal prevented generation. This finding concerns the observable request-to-refusal behaviour; it does not locate the defect in an internal classifier or activation component.

external_assessments.assessment_title: Gemini image generation got it wrong. We'll do better.
external_assessments.scope_note: Google's post-incident explanation covers the same output cluster and its remediation, not every political claim made about the outputs.
external_assessments.assessment_summary: Google concludes that diversity tuning failed to distinguish contexts where diversity should not be introduced and that over-conservative tuning also caused benign refusals.
external_assessments.vigil_comparison_note: VIGIL separately characterises the bounded control as activating outside its valid conditions and does not treat the diversity objective itself as the failure.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: Google acknowledged inaccurate people images and excessive refusals, then temporarily disabled people-image generation. The provider applied a disengagement mechanism for the affected function. The result covers that pause and the provider’s responsibility for it. It does not establish restored calibration after proposed changes.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The provider’s acknowledged unwanted model outcomes and deliberate function pause directly identify disengagement of an inconsistent AI capability under the 2023 AI RMF.
